scorePageTitle: Free Online Sheet Music Editor, No Sign-up · Write Sheet Music
scoreMetaDescription: Free online sheet music editor, no sign-up: write notes, rests, measures, clef and key signature on the staff right in your browser, with nothing to install, and download your score as PDF or MusicXML.
scoreSeoH1: Free online sheet music editor, no sign-up
scoreAboutLead: Write your score straight onto the staff: pick a note value, click where the note goes, done. It is free, runs in your browser and needs no account or install.
scoreShortcutsIntro: Press a figure’s key to pick it, then click on the staff to place it. Press A to deselect the current tool. With figures selected, Shift+D duplicates them right after the last selected one, carrying on into the following measures. These are the keys:
scoreDotBody: Double-click a note to add its dot; double-click again to remove it.
scoreBarBody: Click a single, double or repeat barline to highlight it in yellow, then press Delete to remove it.
scoreTabEditBody: Click a number in the tab and type the new fret; your fingering is saved and the staff does not change. Changing tuning recalculates all frets and replaces manual fingerings while preserving the staff notes. Tuning is saved with this score, and you can undo the change with Ctrl/Cmd+Z.
scoreTabMoveBody: Drag a number to another string or another beat and drop it wherever you want.
scoreFeaturesH2: What you can do with the editor
scoreFeatures: Notes and rests: from whole to thirty-second notes, with dots and accidentals (sharps, flats and naturals).
Measures: pick the time signature (4/4, 3/4, 6/8…) and the editor will not let a measure overflow.
Clef and key signature: treble, bass and C clefs, and any key signature from C♭ to C♯.
Special barlines: double barlines, repeat signs and guitar barre marks.
Settings: piano with a grand staff or guitar with tablature, tempo in the score and the MIDI, and colors to tell voices apart.
Download: export the score as a PDF to print, or as MusicXML to open in MuseScore, Finale, Sibelius or Dorico.
Autosave: your score is kept in your browser, so you can pick it up another day.
scoreHowH2: How to write sheet music online
scoreHow: Type the title and the composer above the score.
Choose a note value or a rest in the toolbar.
Click on the staff to place each note; they group into measures on their own.
Adjust the clef, key signature and barlines if needed.
Download the score as PDF or MusicXML.
scoreFaq: Is it really free to write sheet music here?
Yes. The editor is free, with no usage limits and no account.
Do I need to sign up or install anything?
No. It works in any modern browser on a computer, tablet or phone. Your score is saved in your own browser.
PDF, to print or share, and MusicXML, the standard format that MuseScore, Finale, Sibelius and Dorico open.
Yes. In Settings choose Guitar and you get the guitar treble clef (an octave lower), tablature, repeat signs and barre marks. For piano, the other instrument, every system is a grand staff.

tutorials.metaTitle: Tutorials · Partitura, free online sheet music editor
tutorials.metaDescription: Learn to use the free online sheet music editor, no sign-up, step by step with animations: notes and rests, editing, measures, repeats, dynamics, guitar tablature and files.
tutorials.intro: Partitura is a score editor that runs right in your browser. Here is what is worth knowing before you start.

cards.title: Online, nothing to install
cards.text: Unlike MuseScore, Sibelius, Dorico and other desktop programs, there is nothing to download or install: it runs in the browser, on any computer.

cards.title: No sign-up
cards.text: There is no account to create and no login: open the page and start writing, unlike Noteflight or Flat.io.

cards.title: As many scores as you like
cards.text: You can keep several scores open at once, each in its own tab.

cards.title: Saved in your browser
cards.text: Everything is saved on your device as you write. Nothing is uploaded to any server. To keep or share a score, export it from the menu.

cards.title: Free and ad-free
cards.text: The site is free and has no advertising: no ads or trackers to distract you.

cards.title: Built to be intuitive
cards.text: We work hard to make the interface clear without explanations. Even so, the menu on the left has tutorials for every feature and a guide with all the keyboard shortcuts.

welcome.start: If this is your first time, start with “Getting started” in the menu on the left.

start: How to write your first score online.
features: Notes, measures, clef, key signature, barlines and downloads.
shortcuts: The key for every note, rest and accidental.
dots: Add or remove a dot with a double click.
delete-barline: Select a barline and remove it.
edit-tab: Change a note’s fret without touching the staff.
move-tab: Drag a number to another string or beat.
faq: Free use, download formats and guitar.
notes-rests: Pick a figure, click the staff and keep writing.
accidentals: Alter a note with one key and one click.
select-move: Pick one or several figures and move them without rewriting.
copy: Repeat a motif in a couple of keystrokes.
tuplets: Turn consecutive figures into a triplet, a quintuplet and more.
ties: Join two notes with a tie or group eighth notes with a beam.
signatures: Change the meter, clef or key anywhere in the score.
measures: Build the structure of the score measure by measure.
repeats: Repeat barlines, da capo, segno and endings.
tab-toggle: A tab under every system, with the fingering already worked out.
refinger: Move a note to another string
Play the same sound on a different string.
barre: Mark a barre and its fret over the notes it covers.
settings: Piano or guitar, tempo, and which tool groups to show.
files: Open a MusicXML or MIDI file and download your score as PDF, MusicXML or MIDI.
scores: Work on several scores at once; everything saves itself in your browser.

steps: Pick a figure in the palette or press its key: <kbd>1</kbd> (32nd) to <kbd>6</kbd> (whole) for notes, and <kbd>Q</kbd> to <kbd>Y</kbd> for rests.
Click the staff: the height of the click is the pitch and the horizontal position is the time. You can also drag the figure from the palette to its place.
The tool stays active after each figure, so you can write a whole phrase without picking it again. Eighth notes and shorter ones beam themselves.
Press <kbd>A</kbd> or <kbd>Esc</kbd> to drop the tool and go back to selecting figures.
notes-rests.tip: If a figure does not fit in what is left of the measure, the editor tells you and does not place it.

steps: Press <kbd>S</kbd> for a sharp, <kbd>B</kbd> for a flat or <kbd>C</kbd> for a natural. They are in the palette too.
Click the note you want to alter: the sign appears to its left.
Dots work the same way: press <kbd>P</kbd> and click the note, or double-click it.
Click a figure to select it. <kbd>Shift</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> or <kbd>Cmd</kbd> adds more. Dragging from an empty spot on the staff encloses them in a rectangle.
<kbd>↑</kbd> and <kbd>↓</kbd> raise or lower the selection by one staff step; <kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> move to the next figure. You can also drag the figures elsewhere.
<kbd>Delete</kbd> or <kbd>Backspace</kbd> removes them. <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>Z</kbd> undoes the last change and <kbd>Esc</kbd> clears the selection.
Select one or more figures and press <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>D</kbd>: they are copied right after the last selected one, carrying on into the measures that follow.

To bring them somewhere else, copy with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd>, click the destination measure and paste with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> + <kbd>V</kbd>. It works between open scores too.
copy.tip: Hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> while pasting to paste only the figures, without clef, key or meter changes.

steps: Select 2 to 9 consecutive figures of the same value, for example three eighth notes.
A menu appears over the selection with the group that matches how many there are: triplet, duplet, quadruplet, quintuplet, sextuplet, septuplet, octuplet or nonuplet.
Pick the group: the figures shrink to fit the same time and the number shows above them.
To undo it, select the group and choose Remove triplet (or whichever applies) from the same menu.
Select two consecutive notes with Shift+click. In the menu over them choose Tie: if they sound the same a tie is drawn, otherwise a slur.
To remove it, select the same notes and choose Remove tie.
Beams work the same way: select consecutive figures and choose Beam to join them or Unbeam to split the beam. If you do nothing, the editor groups them by the meter.
Click the meter number, the clef or the key signature spot at the start of a system.
Pick the value in the menu: meter (4/4, 3/4, 6/8…), clef (treble, guitar treble, bass, alto or tenor) or key (from C♭ to C♯). For clef and key, confirm with Apply.
The change holds from that measure until the next change, so you can switch meter or key mid-piece.
signatures.tip: If the figures you already wrote do not fit the new meter, the editor asks you to remove or move some before changing it.

steps: Click an empty part of a measure to select it: two + buttons appear at its edges to insert a measure before or after.
At the end of each system, the + and − buttons add or remove a measure. To add another system use the button under the score.
Hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> and drag a measure to move it elsewhere.
Drag a barline sideways to make a measure wider or narrower.
In the palette, pick Repeat start, Repeat end or Double bar and click the measure where it goes.
For jumps, pick Da capo, Dal segno, Segno, First ending or Second ending and click the measure: the sign sits above the staff.
To delete a barline or a sign, click it to select it and press <kbd>Delete</kbd>.
In the palette pick Crescendo or Diminuendo and click the note where it starts: the hairpin runs to the end of the measure.
Click it to select it: two handles appear under its ends to widen or shorten it.
Each end has a spot for a dynamic, showing the suggested one (p → f on a crescendo). Click it to choose another, from ppp to fff, or none.
Press the TAB button in the palette: a six-string tablature appears under every system.

The first tablature shows the string names, from highest to lowest (E B G D A E in standard tuning). Click these names to choose Standard, Drop D, Double Drop D, DADGAD, Open D or Open G. The menu lists strings from lowest to highest.
Changing tuning recalculates all frets and replaces manual fingerings while preserving the staff notes. Tuning is saved with this score, and you can undo the change with Ctrl/Cmd+Z.
The editor picks the most comfortable fingering by itself: it keeps the hand in one position, avoids jumps and does not reuse a string for different notes.
The staff does not change when you touch the tablature. Press the button again to hide it.
tab-toggle.tip: The next two guides explain how to change a number or move it to another string.

steps: In the tablature, click the number of the note you want to move.
Press <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>↑</kbd> to move it to the string above or <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>↓</kbd> for the string below. The fret adjusts itself so it sounds the same.
Changing tuning recalculates all frets and replaces manual fingerings while preserving the staff notes. Tuning is saved with this score, and you can undo the change with Ctrl/Cmd+Z.
refinger.tip: Only the fingering changes: the note on the staff and the sound stay the same.

steps: In the palette pick Barre and click the note where it starts (or anywhere in the measure to cover it from the beginning).
A C appears with a field for the fret: type a number from 1 to 24 and press Enter.
Drag the handles at its ends, or use <kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> on them, to change how far it reaches. Clear the number to remove the barre.
Open Settings with the cog, the first tool in the sidebar. They apply to the score you are looking at, are saved with it, and can be undone with Ctrl/Cmd + Z.

Instrument: with Piano every system is a grand staff, treble clef above and bass clef below joined by a brace, and TAB and barre are hidden. With Guitar there is a single staff in guitar treble clef, and the TAB button and barre appear. Switching between them deletes nothing: whatever is hidden stays saved.
Tempo: the slider goes from 20 to 300 quarter notes per minute. It is written as a metronome mark above the first measure and sets the speed of the exported MIDI. No marking removes it.
Tools: turn Repeats, Dynamics and Voices on or off to show or hide their buttons in the sidebar. Hiding a group does not delete what you already wrote.
Voices: with Voices on, each voice gets a color (1 to 4) and a legend appears to the left of the brace. In the legend you choose which voices to color; no note is ever hidden.

Grand staff: each staff has its own notes, rests, voices and clef (the clef menu says which one it changes). Measures, key signature, time signature, barlines, repeats and tempo are shared by both. Dynamics and hairpins are written between the two.
settings.tip: On export, piano goes into MusicXML as a single part with two staves, and in MIDI each staff plays on its own channel.

steps: Open the ☰ menu at the top right.
Load file… opens a MusicXML (.musicxml, .xml) or a MIDI (.mid) file and turns it into a new score.
Export downloads the score: PDF to print, MusicXML for MuseScore, Finale, Sibelius or Dorico, and MIDI to play it in any program.
Open scores are the tabs at the top. The + button creates a new empty one, and clicking a tab takes you back to the one you left.
Everything saves itself in your browser as you write: come back another day and it is all there. Nothing is uploaded to any server.
The trash button clears the score you are looking at, and asks for confirmation first.
scores.tip: Clearing your browser data loses the scores: export as MusicXML the ones you want to keep.

terms.metaDescription: Terms of use for Partitura, the free online score editor with no sign-up: using the service, your scores, intellectual property and liability.
sections: By using Partitura you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, do not use the service.
Partitura is a free score editor that runs in your browser. No sign-up is needed. We may change, suspend or remove features at any time, with or without notice.

The scores you write are stored only in your browser (local storage) and are not sent to any server. Because we hold no copy, we cannot recover them: clearing your browser data or switching devices loses them. Export your work (PDF, MusicXML or MIDI) to keep it.

Your compositions and arrangements are yours; we only provide the tool to write them. You are responsible for having the rights to any content you load or transcribe, such as copyrighted works by others. The design, code and brand of Partitura belong to their authors; the third-party software we use keeps its own licences.
Please do not use the service for unlawful activity, to try to compromise or overload it, or to infringe the rights of others.

Partitura is provided "as is" and "as available", without warranties of any kind. We do not promise that it is error-free, that it will run without interruption, or that its output is fit for a particular purpose, such as professional engraving or printing.
To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for loss of data, work or income, or for any other damage arising from using the service or being unable to use it.
We may update these terms. The date above shows the latest revision; continuing to use Partitura after a change means you accept it.
